questions.text: In which country can you find this famous statue?
questions.funFact: Christ the Redeemer stands 30 meters tall and was completed in 1931.

questions.text: This flaming crater is known as the 'Door to Hell'. Where is it?
questions.funFact: The Darvaza gas crater has been burning continuously since 1971.

questions.text: Which country is home to this ancient temple?
questions.funFact: Borobudur is the world's largest Buddhist temple, built in the 9th century.

questions.text: This iconic mountain is a symbol of which country?
questions.funFact: Mount Fuji is 3,776 meters high and last erupted in 1707.

questions.text: This colorful town with blue and white houses is in which country?
questions.funFact: Sidi Bou Said's blue and white color scheme was established by a French baron in 1915.

questions.text: These rock-hewn churches are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Where are they?
questions.funFact: The 11 churches of Lalibela were carved from solid rock in the 12th-13th century.

questions.text: This grand mosque is one of the largest in the world. Where is it?
questions.funFact: The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque can accommodate over 40,000 worshippers.

questions.text: These mysterious stone statues are found on which island?
questions.funFact: The Moai statues were carved by the Rapa Nui people between 1250 and 1500 AD.

questions.text: This ancient citadel lit up at night is in which city?
questions.funFact: The Acropolis of Athens was built in the 5th century BC during the Golden Age of Pericles.

questions.text: This double-pipe wind instrument is traditional to which country?
questions.funFact: The arghul has been played in Egypt for over 5,000 years.

questions.text: This plucked string instrument called the kantele is from which country?
questions.funFact: The kantele is the national instrument of Finland, featured in the epic Kalevala.

questions.text: The djembe drum originates from which West African country?
questions.funFact: The djembe originated with the Mandinka people around the 12th century.

questions.text: This triangular string instrument called the balalaika is from which country?
questions.funFact: The balalaika became a symbol of Russian folk music in the 18th century.

questions.text: The sitar is an iconic instrument from which country?
questions.funFact: Ravi Shankar popularized the sitar worldwide through his collaboration with The Beatles.

questions.text: The bagpipes (cornemuse) are most associated with which country?
questions.funFact: The Great Highland Bagpipe has been used in Scottish military for over 500 years.

questions.text: This two-stringed bowed instrument called the erhu is from which country?
questions.funFact: The erhu has been played for over 1,000 years and is often called the Chinese violin.

questions.text: This burrito is a traditional dish from which country?
questions.funFact: The burrito is believed to have originated in Northern Mexico in the 19th century.

questions.text: This glass noodle stir-fry dish called Japchae is from which country?
questions.funFact: Japchae was originally created for a royal banquet in the 17th century.

questions.text: Fish and chips is a beloved national dish of which country?
questions.funFact: The first fish and chip shop in the UK opened in the 1860s.

questions.text: Falafels are a popular street food originating from which region?
questions.funFact: Falafels are one of the most widely consumed Middle Eastern foods worldwide.

questions.text: This spiced rice dish called Kabsa is the national dish of which country?
questions.funFact: Kabsa is the most popular dish in Saudi Arabia, often served for gatherings.

questions.text: This black bean stew called Feijoada is the national dish of which country?
questions.funFact: Feijoada is traditionally served on Wednesdays and Saturdays in Brazilian restaurants.

questions.text: Bunny chow — a hollowed bread loaf filled with curry — is from which country?
questions.funFact: Bunny chow was created by the Indian community in Durban in the 1940s.

questions.text: These meatballs (köttbullar) are a famous dish from which country?
questions.funFact: Swedish meatballs became globally famous thanks to IKEA's food courts.

questions.text: Poutine — fries with cheese curds and gravy — is from which country?
questions.funFact: Poutine originated in rural Québec in the late 1950s.

questions.text: This tagine dish with chicken and olives is from which country?
questions.funFact: The tagine is both the name of the dish and the conical clay pot it's cooked in.

questions.text: This layered rice and lentil dish called Koshari is the national dish of which country?
questions.funFact: Koshari is Egypt's most popular street food, mixing Italian, Indian and Arab influences.

questions.text: This communal hot pot is a traditional way of eating in which country?
questions.funFact: Hot pot has been a Chinese tradition for over 1,000 years, especially popular in Sichuan.
